gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 12V split-phase unit it called 'best value' (SunGold 4000W, shown at $624) costs $936 on SunGold's store today and needs 240VAC input to charge and pass power through, so it can't charge from a 120V-only source such as RV shore power or a 120V generator. Charging from 120V takes the AIMS 120VAC-input version, which costs $1,949 at Outbound Power and has a 70 A charger. AIMS's 240VAC-input version costs $1,695 and has a 115 A charger.
standout_why: I compared against Victron's help-me-choose page and its MultiPlus-II 2x120V page, the two pages ChatGPT cited, plus the Victron PDFs and dealer pages in its results. They cover only Victron and say nothing about SunGold or AIMS units or what AC input their chargers need. ChatGPT's answer listed SunGold at $624 and AIMS at $1,949 without explaining why AIMS costs about twice as much: the AIMS version it showed charges from 120V, and SunGold's does not. The SunGold price it showed is also $312 below SunGold's own store today.
decides: It splits the pick by charging source. A 12V buyer who charges from 30 A/120V RV or marine shore power or a 120V generator should skip the SunGold 4000W, because it needs 240VAC input. That buyer needs the AIMS PICOGLF4012120240VS at $1,949 (charges from 120V at 70 A) or the AIMS 3000W split-phase inverter-only unit at $880 with separate charging. A cabin or home buyer with a 240V generator or grid feed should take the SunGold 4000W at $936 from SunGold or the AIMS 240VAC-input unit at $1,695. The Victron MultiPlus-II 2x120V ($1,190) doesn't fit anyone who needs 240V loads on battery, because Victron says it makes 240V only when a split-phase source is connected. Dealectric's Sun Gold 6000W split-phase inverter fails the question's 12V requirement: its store listing is titled 24V/48V, and our catalog has it as the 48V model.
